relations.evidence: yadā nepālabhūpālānantamadhyebhidhāvati ... kāyasthodayaharṣeṇa harṣeṇa likhitaṃ drutaṃ

notes: The manuscript was copied in VS 1985 (1928 CE) from an earlier palm-leaf exemplar written in Newari script ('nevārākṣaralikhitaprācīnatāḍapatrapustakād udhṛtya 1985 saṃvatsare likhitam idam'). The catalogue accidentally entered 'VS 1985' under Place of Copying. The exemplar's colophon was copied verbatim, which records the scribe Kāyastha Udayaharṣa on Kārttika kṛṣṇa 2, Tuesday, and possibly refers to King Anantamalla of Nepal ('nepālabhūpālānanta...'), though this could also form part of a verse chronogram.
